# Browser playback fixtures

These six files are original synthetic test media generated from FFmpeg's `lavfi` sine and test-pattern sources. They contain no imported recording, song, video, or other third-party creative material. The clips are about 15 seconds long so browser tests can seek and confirm playback continues afterward.

Generated with FFmpeg 9.0.1 (`libmp3lame`, `libopus`, `libaom-av1`):

| File | Streams | Duration |
|---|---|---:|
| `browser-e2e-tone.mp3` | MP3, mono, 48 kHz, 96 kbit/s | 15.000 s |
| `browser-e2e-opus.ogg` | Opus, mono, 48 kHz, Ogg | 15.007 s |
| `browser-e2e-opus.webm` | Opus, mono, 48 kHz, WebM | 15.008 s |
| `browser-e2e-opus.mp4` | Opus, mono, 48 kHz, MP4 | 15.000 s |
| `browser-e2e-av1-opus.webm` | AV1 Main 8-bit 32×24 at 10 fps plus Opus mono 48 kHz | 15.008 s |
| `browser-e2e-av1-opus.mp4` | Same AV1+Opus streams remuxed to MP4 | 15.001 s |

From the repository root, the fixtures can be regenerated with:

```sh
f=packages/worker/test/fixtures
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i 'sine=frequency=997:duration=15:sample_rate=48000' -c:a libmp3lame -b:a 96k -metadata title='Browser E2E Tone' -metadata artist='Original Test Fixture' -y "$f/browser-e2e-tone.mp3"
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i 'sine=frequency=659:duration=15:sample_rate=48000' -c:a libopus -b:a 48k -metadata title='Browser E2E Opus Ogg' -metadata artist='Original Test Fixture' -y "$f/browser-e2e-opus.ogg"
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i 'sine=frequency=523:duration=15:sample_rate=48000' -c:a libopus -b:a 48k -metadata title='Browser E2E Opus WebM' -y "$f/browser-e2e-opus.webm"
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i 'sine=frequency=784:duration=15:sample_rate=48000' -c:a libopus -b:a 48k -metadata title='Browser E2E Opus MP4' -movflags +faststart -y "$f/browser-e2e-opus.mp4"
ffmpeg -f lavfi -i 'testsrc2=size=32x24:rate=10:duration=15' -f lavfi -i 'sine=frequency=440:duration=15:sample_rate=48000' -c:v libaom-av1 -cpu-used 8 -crf 45 -b:v 0 -c:a libopus -b:a 48k -shortest -y "$f/browser-e2e-av1-opus.webm"
ffmpeg -i "$f/browser-e2e-av1-opus.webm" -map 0 -c copy -movflags +faststart -y "$f/browser-e2e-av1-opus.mp4"
```

Codec encoders can produce slightly different container sizes across FFmpeg versions. The browser test compares downloaded and ranged bytes against each checked-in fixture itself, not against a regenerated byte sequence.
